sentences.text: This appeal is filed by the State being aggrieved of judgment dated 18.10.2023 passed by the Fifth Additional Sessions Judge, Chhindwara in Sessions Trial No.79/2022 acquitting the accused persons namely, Laxmi, Lavkesh @ Lokesh and Anita from the charges of Section 498A of the Indian Penal Code, 1860 and Section 3/4 of the Dowry Prohibition Act, 1961 Learned Government Advocate for the State reading the evidence of the prosecutrix (PW.1) submits that on the basis of her statement, the conviction should have been recorded by the Trial Court.
It is evident that the allegation on the respondent/accused Anita is that she had alleged about the lack of duty in the complainant and had said that she should not be kept in the house.
As far as Nilesh is concerned, the allegation against him is that he had asked the complainant to take her clothes and leave the house.
There are no allegations of demand of dowry either on Anita, Nilesh 2 CRA-1383-2024 or Laxmi.
No piece of evidence is available on record to show that they ever demanded any dowry form the complainant or her relatives.
In view of such facts, the acquittal recorded by the Trial Court cannot be faulted with.

This appeal has been filed in a mechanical manner without application of mind though the State professes itself to be a champion of curtailing unnecessary litigation for which they have laid down a litigation policy but it appears that the State itself is the biggest violator of its own litigation policy and is involved in filing unnecessary appeals.
There are no grounds to show indulgence in this appeal.
